speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the characteristics of your neck swelling, including its duration, consistency, tenderness, and whether you have experienced any recent infections, fever, or weight loss.

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck (from the nape of the neck) to regional lymph nodes, given the patient's history of colon cancer, though thyroid cancer or lymphoma must be considered. I will now request imaging and further tests to confirm.

REQUEST TEST: Thyroid_Ultrasound, Neck_CTA, and Serum_TSH_with_Thyroid_Antibodies.
REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_CTA, Thyroid_Ultrasound.
